title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 107: The Kauri Forests of New Zealand
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 107 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Kauri Forests of New Zealand

Paragraph 1. Giant kauri trees grow in the northern forests of New Zealand. They are among the biggest and oldest trees on Earth. Some kauri trees grow over fifty metres tall, and some live for more than two thousand years. The local Māori people deeply respected living kauri trees. They never cut down live trees. Instead, they used only fallen wood to build large ocean canoes, and they took tree bark to make dark ink for traditional skin drawings.

Paragraph 2. Everything changed when European settlers arrived in the late 1700s. British navy captains saw that kauri trunks were very tall and straight. They wanted kauri wood to make tall masts for sailing ships. Soon, logging companies cut down huge numbers of trees. Because the giant logs were too heavy for farm animals to pull down steep hills, workers built big wooden dams across rivers. When the water became full, they opened the gates to wash hundreds of logs down to the sea.

Paragraph 3. From 1870 to 1920, thousands of workers also searched for kauri gum under the wet ground. Kauri gum is hard, old tree juice that sat in swampy soil for thousands of years. Workers pushed long metal spears into the soft mud to find hard pieces of gum, and then dug them out with spades. Factories in Europe and North America bought this gum to make shiny wood coatings, paints, and floor coverings.

Paragraph 4. By 1950, heavy logging and digging had destroyed over ninety-five percent of the old kauri forests. Today, a dangerous plant illness called kauri dieback threatens the last trees. The illness moves from tree to tree in tiny drops of mud on hikers' shoes. Park officers now require every visitor to scrub and clean all dirt off their boots at forest gates.

groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

q5.text: Some kauri trees can live for more than two thousand years.

steps: Đoạn 1: "...some live for more than two thousand years."

q6.text: Māori workers cut down healthy living kauri trees to build their boats.

q7.text: Today, over half of New Zealand's original kauri forests are still standing.

steps: Đoạn 4: Hơn 95% rừng nguyên sinh đã bị phá hủy (destroyed over ninety-five percent), không thể còn quá một nửa.

q8.text: Tickets to enter kauri forests are very expensive for tourists.

steps: Đoạn 4: Bài chỉ nói du khách phải rửa sạch giày ở cổng rừng, không đề cập giá vé.
